newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan shares Tietmeyer views on currencies--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan shares Tietmeyer views on currencies--MOF.

text.p: Japan shares views expressed by the head of Germany's central bank on currencies, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Friday.

Asked whether Japan agreed with remarks by Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer overnight, Mitsuzuka said: "I agree with Mr Tietmeyer's views," adding that it was not desirable for exchange rates to move excessively.

Tietmeyer said at a news conference on Thursday that the mark's current level correctly reflects economic fundamentals. Tietmeyer said the Bundesbank did not want a weak mark and remained interested in having a strong mark.
Mitsuzuka reiterated that Japan would take decisive steps to tackle excessive movements in currency rates.
He also said the Group of Seven (G7) nations would cooperate in taking measures against such excessive movements, as agreed at their meeting in Berlin in February.

Asked whether he expected the United States to express concern over Japan's trade surplus with the U.S., Mitsuzuka said: "If it (the surplus) is within acceptable levels taking into account the economies of the two nations, then it is not a problem."
Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and President Bill Clinton are to meet in Washington next week.
Mitsuzuka said that although Japanese exports of cars had increased due to the weakening of the yen, imports into Japan continued to be at high levels.

The Finance Ministry said on Thursday that Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus slid 26.8 percent in March from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen, but that the trade surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 11.2 percent in March from a year earlier to 379.83 billion yen.
